# Phase 0 spike results (2026-10-07)

**Machine:** M-series Mac with 8 performance and 2 efficiency cores, 32 GB RAM, macOS 26.6.2, Xcode SDK 27.0, Swift 6.4.
**Model server:** mlx-vlm 0.7.6.
**Rust:** 1.99 (cargo 1.99.0).

**Test page:** `spike/fixtures/legal.pdf`, generated by `spike/make_fixture.py`. It is a synthetic one-page complaint with:
- pleading line numbers 1–28;
- a caption title;
- numbered paragraphs and a lettered sub-list;
- a 4×3 table;
- the footer "COMPLAINT - Page 1 of 14";
- the Bates number `SMITH000123`.

## 0b. Swift ↔ Rust bridge (Option A works)

- **Build.** `bridge/` is a SwiftPM static library with `@_cdecl` exports. `build.rs` runs `swift build -c release` and links against the toolchain's `lib/swift/macosx` plus the SDK's `usr/lib/swift`, with rpath `/usr/lib/swift`. Deployment target 26.0 is set in both `Package.swift` and `.cargo/config.toml`. It linked on the first attempt.
- **Async bridging.** The async `RecognizeDocumentsRequest.perform(on: URL)` call runs inside `Task.detached`, and the C caller blocks on a `DispatchSemaphore`. This works when called from Rust `std::thread`s.
- **API, confirmed from the SDK `.swiftinterface`.** `DocumentObservation.document` is a `Container` with these members:
  - `title: Text?`
  - `paragraphs: [Text]`
  - `tables: [Table]`; a table has `rows: [[Cell]]`, and each `Cell` has `content: Container`, `rowRange` and `columnRange`.
  - `lists: [List]`; a list has `items: [Item]` with `markerString` and `itemString`.
  - `barcodes`.
  - `NormalizedRegion` is a typealias of `ContoursObservation.Contour`. Use `normalizedPath.boundingBox`, which has a bottom-left origin.
- **Thread safety and scaling** (same 300 DPI page, N concurrent calls):

  | Threads | Wall | Pages/s | Outputs identical |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 0.63 s | 1.6 | yes |
  | 2 | 0.68 s | 2.9 | yes |
  | 4 | 0.88 s | 4.5 | yes |
  | 8 | 1.20 s | 6.7 | yes |
  | 12 | 1.84 s | 6.5 | yes |
  | 16 | 2.34 s | 6.8 | yes |

  Throughput levels off at 8 threads, the number of performance cores. **Default `--jobs` for `apple` = performance-core count** is confirmed.
- **Quality issues to fix in Phase 2:**
  - Errors: `cv`→`cr` in the case number, `$`→`S` in one table cell, and `21` read as a Korean glyph.
  - Fixes: pin `recognitionLanguages` to `en-US`, disable `automaticallyDetectLanguage`, and keep language correction on.
  - Pleading line numbers come back as separate tiny paragraphs in the left margin, so they are easy to filter by bbox.
  - Lists lose their markers unless `markerString` is prepended.
  - The table had one spurious empty column; trim it.
  - `paragraphs`, `lists` and `tables` are separate arrays. Reading order must be rebuilt by bbox, and paragraphs that overlap a table or list must be dropped. The bridge already does both.

## 0a. Model servers (`mlx_vlm.server`)

**Flags** confirmed with `--help` on 0.7.6: `--host --port --model --trust-remote-code --max-tokens --max-num-seqs --max-kv-size --log-level`.
- The server uses **continuous batching**.
- `--max-num-seqs` limits how many sequences run at once; the default is unlimited.
- `--trust-remote-code` was **not needed** for any engine. mlx-vlm has native model code for all three.

**Prompts** were taken verbatim from upstream:
- olmOCR: `build_no_anchoring_v4_yaml_prompt()` from `allenai/olmocr@8ef7f808`, `olmocr/prompts/prompts.py`. This is olmOCR 2's own no-anchor prompt.
- dots: `prompt_layout_all_en` and `prompt_ocr` from `rednote-hilab/dots.mocr@05196189`, `dots_mocr/utils/prompts.py`. These are identical in wording to `dots.ocr@b06a7810`.
- dots.mocr is rednote-hilab's successor repo. Its HF tags include `dots_ocr`.
- Copies are in `spike/upstream/`.

### Results

Single page, temperature 0. Images are olmOCR at 1288 px on the longest side, and the others at 200 DPI (1700×2200).

| Engine / weights | Ready (`/health`, real probe) | s/page | ×2 conc. | ×4 conc. | Peak RSS (psutil, **undercounts**) | Quality on test page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PaddleOCR-VL 1.6 4bit (`mlx-community/PaddleOCR-VL-1.6-4bit`) | 6 s, 8.4 s | 2.4 | 1.15× | 1.25× | 1.5 GB | Words perfect. Table comes out as space-aligned text. Footer and Bates kept |
| PaddleOCR-VL 1.6 bf16 (`PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL-1.6`) | –, 5.1 s | 2.6 | 0.91× | 1.21× | 2.4 GB | Same words as 4bit, with better paragraph joining |
| dots.mocr 8bit (`mlx-community/dots.mocr-8bit`) | 6.3 s, 8.5 s | 34.4 | 1.09× | 1.12× | 3.3 GB | Perfect. JSON array of `{bbox, category, text}`. Table as HTML. Footer and Bates labelled `Page-footer` |
| olmOCR 2 8bit (`mlx-community/olmOCR-2-7B-1025-8bit`) | 6.8 s, 9.5 s | 15.9 | 1.35× | 1.42× | 6.5 GB | Perfect body. YAML front-matter. Table as HTML. **Drops the footer and Bates number** |

- **Paddle table mode.** `Table Recognition:` on a crop returns OTSL tokens: `<fcel>cell…<nl>`. We need an OTSL→GFM converter.
- **Determinism.**
  - Sequential repeats were byte-identical for every engine.
  - Under concurrency, Paddle and dots sometimes change **whitespace and line-joining only**. The words did not change.
- **Cancellation.**
  - The server does not cancel abandoned requests; they run to completion.
  - For a fast model this is harmless, because continuous batching serves new requests alongside: a short request ran in 0.24 s on Paddle.
  - For dots, a short request sent after abandoning a large-prefill request **waited 26 s**. Restart-on-timeout is justified.
- **`/health` vs readiness.** `/health` answered 2–3 s before a real generation succeeded, so the probe request is needed.

### Memory, re-measured with `vmmap --summary` (physical footprint peak, after one real page)

psutil RSS missed Metal and unified-memory allocations. These are the real numbers:

| Engine | Weights on disk | Physical footprint peak |
|---|---|---|
| olmOCR 2 8bit | 8.8 GiB | **10.9 GB** |
| dots.mocr 8bit | 4.1 GiB | **7.3 GB** |
| PaddleOCR-VL 1.6 bf16 | 1.8 GiB | **3.8 GB** |

### Apple Vision accuracy matrix (`cargo run --release --example vision_bench -- <img> matrix`)

The checks are exact matches for the case number, all four dollar amounts and the Bates number.

| Render | correction on | correction off |
|---|---|---|
| 150 DPI | all ok | all ok |
| 200 DPI | all ok | all ok |
| 250 DPI | misses `$48,250.00` | misses `$48,250.00` |
| 300 DPI | misses case no. + `$22,375.50` | misses `$22,375.50` |
| 400 DPI | misses case no. + 2 amounts | misses case no. + 2 amounts |

- **Language correction caused** the `cv`→`cr` error at 300 DPI.
- Auto-detect vs `en-US` made no difference here, apart from the Korean-glyph error earlier.
- **Higher DPI is not better.** Vision does best at about 150–200 DPI.
- This is one page, so Phase 2 must tune it on the eval set.
- **Idea for legal accuracy:** run Vision at 2 DPIs and flag pages where numeric tokens disagree. It is cheap, at about 0.15 s per pass.

## Decisions fed back into PLAN.md

1. **`--jobs` defaults.** `apple` gets the performance-core count.
   - **Model engines get 1, with `--max-num-seqs 1`.**
   - Concurrency gained only 0.91–1.42×, and Paddle bf16 was slower with 2 jobs.
   - Batching changed outputs on 2 of 3 engines. Only whitespace changed on this page, but batch-dependent numerics could flip a digit.
   - Sequential runs were byte-identical. Rendering and the Apple side-pass still run in parallel with the model request.
   - `--jobs >1` on a model engine is allowed, with a printed reproducibility note.
2. **Paddle.** Default to `PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL-1.6` bf16. It is only 2.4 GB, needs no conversion, and joins paragraphs better.
   - Full-page `OCR:` is accurate enough, so the plan is simplified: run full-page `OCR:`, and use Apple Vision **only to find tables**, which are cropped and sent with `Table Recognition:` (OTSL→GFM).
   - This replaces cropping every block.
3. **Bates and footers.** olmOCR drops them. For every model engine, a fast Apple Vision pass (about 0.15 s per page in parallel) extracts header and footer lines and Bates numbers for page markers. The model output is still used for the body.
4. **Restart-on-timeout** stays (§5.4), with the dots measurement above as justification.
5. **Determinism criterion.** At default settings, output is byte-identical across runs for every engine, except the `generated:` front-matter timestamp.
6. **RAM** (vmmap). olmOCR 8-bit 10.9 GB, dots 7.3 GB, Paddle 3.8 GB.
   - Setup recommends `--quant 4bit` for olmOCR below 24 GB of RAM.
   - It refuses 8-bit below 16 GB unless `--force` is given.
8. **Apple defaults.** Render at 200 DPI, language correction off, `en-US`. The Phase 2 exit criterion is that the case number and every dollar amount on the fixture are exact.
7. **Throughput** for setting expectations on a 300-page scanned filing, at default `--jobs 1` for model engines:
   - Apple: about 1 minute.
   - Paddle: about 12 minutes.
   - olmOCR: about 80 minutes.
   - dots: about 2.9 hours.
   - Phase 6 should test lower DPI for dots, because 5k prompt tokens per page makes prefill dominate.

## Phase 2b pre-check: deposition transcripts (2026-10-07)

**Setup.** `examples/crop_probe.rs` runs the production `RecognizeDocumentsRequest` on crops. `spike/transcript_qa.py` runs PaddleOCR-VL through `mlx_vlm.server`. The fixtures are:
- `spike/heldout/four_up.pdf`: 4-up, Courier 6.5 pt, 25 numbered `Q.` lines per mini-page;
- `spike/out/transcript_full.pdf`: one full-size page, Courier 12 pt, alternating `Q.`/`A.`.

**Apple Vision.**

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| 4-up, one mini-page cropped | Text mostly right, but the region becomes a 25-row "table". `Q.` is misread as `l.`, `e.` or `2.` |
| 4-up crops, by DPI | Exact `Q. Question k.n…` lines: 200 DPI 17/100, 300 DPI 30/100, 400 DPI 41/100, 600 DPI 34/100. Language correction and custom words `Q.`/`A.` make no difference |
| Full-size transcript at 200 DPI | 19/25 correct Q/A markers, and **every line number dropped**: the number column comes back as empty table cells |

**PaddleOCR-VL 1.6 bf16, prompt `OCR:`.**

| Input | Exact (line number + Q/A + text) |
|---|---|
| Full-size transcript | 25/25 |
| 4-up quadrant crops | 100/100 |
| 4-up **whole page, uncropped** | 100/100 |

**Conclusion.** Region detection cannot fix Apple Vision on transcripts. The recognizer itself loses line numbers and Q/A markers, which are what page:line citation depends on. PaddleOCR-VL handles them with no layout help.

## Paddle engine spike (2026-10-07, production render path)

**Setup.** PNGs come from `examples/render_png`, which uses the bridge's `ocr_bridge_render_png`. The model is `PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL-1.6` (bf16), with prompt `OCR:` and `--max-num-seqs 1`. Scripts: `spike/paddle_spike.py`, `spike/paddle_crops.py`.

1. **Legal fixtures, full page.** `legal.pdf` and `legal_scan.pdf` at 150, 200 and 300 DPI: the case number, all 4 amounts and the Bates number are exact. Paddle shows **no `$`→`S` error**, so the currency fix stays Apple-only.
2. **Columns, full page.**
   - `two_column.pdf`: 30/30 in order.
   - Held-out seeds 0–2: perfect on `two_col_title_footer`, `signature_block` and `block_quote`, and 80–100% on `lower_half_columns`.
   - **`narrow_unequal` collapses: 10–28 of 28–42 lines.** Paddle garbles the dense narrow columns and then loops ("…obligation in the part of the case under the…") until `max_tokens` 4096. Seven of the roughly 40 requests hit 4096 tokens.
   - **With the Phase 2b column crops, the same page gives 42/42 in order and both requests finish with `stop`.** So Paddle uses the 2b regions too.
3. **Table bands.** On `legal_scan.pdf`, bands above and below the table run with `OCR:` and the table crop runs with `Table Recognition:`. All tokens are exact. The table comes back as OTSL (`<fcel>cell…<nl>`), which converts to GFM. Banding drops the blank lines between paragraphs in the band text.
4. **Timing.**
   - Prefill is about 990 tok/s; a full page is about 1253 prompt tokens, so about 1.3 s.
   - Decode is about 250 tok/s normally and about 218 tok/s on long outputs.
   - A normal page generates 150–800 tokens, 1–4 s in total.
   - A runaway to 4096 tokens takes about 19 s.
   - **Timeout:** 45 s per request, derived as 2 × (prefill + 4096/218).

## olmOCR and dots engine spike (2026-10-07)

**Setup.** Server: `ocr server setup` and `ocr server start` in a temp state dir on a free port (mlx-vlm 0.7.6, `--max-num-seqs 1`), one server at a time. Images come from the production render path (`examples/render_png`, which now takes `[crop|-] [max_side] [rotation]`); crop rects come from the production plan (`examples/crop_plan`, the same `region_specs` the engines use). Script: `spike/olmdots_spike.py`. Fixtures: `legal_scan`, `two_column`, `narrow_unequal_seed2` (with `expected.json`), `transcript_full`, `four_up`, and the new image-only `legal_scan_rot90.png`.

**Load caveat.** `pgrep -fl "ocr scan|mlx_vlm"` was empty before each run. Other users' desktop apps were running (load average 1.1 to 3.7 across the session, with no process above 6% CPU), so the rates below are for a nearly idle machine; a busy machine would be slower.

### Render path: max-side and rotation

`render_png` gained `max_side` and `rotation` in the Swift bridge and `vision::render_png_fit` (`render_png` keeps its signature and path, so Paddle and Apple are untouched).
- `max_side` ignores the DPI and sizes the **crop**, if any, to exactly that many pixels on its longest side. A PDF is scaled to the target while it is rendered (no DPI derived in Rust, no downscale of a 2200 px page); a raster input skips the `11 x dpi` cap; a final exact resample guards the +-1 px that an integral crop rect leaves. Measured: `legal_scan` 995x1288, `two_column` crop 622x1288.
- `rotation` is counter-clockwise (0, 90, 180, 270), checked by looking at the PNG: the top of the page moves to the left for 90.
- Rotation semantics, from `allenai/olmocr@8ef7f8085aeea5a7b857f2ff4a032f3a8f0fcfa2`, `olmocr/pipeline.py`: `process_page` sets `cumulative_rotation = (cumulative_rotation + rotation_correction) % 360` when `is_rotation_valid` is false, and `build_page_query` turns the freshly rendered image with PIL `Image.transpose(ROTATE_90 | ROTATE_180 | ROTATE_270)`. PIL's `ROTATE_90` is a counter-clockwise quarter turn, although the front-matter schema says "degree of clockwise rotation needed". The code is what counts, and the real model agrees: `legal_scan_rot90.png` (the page turned 90 degrees clockwise) comes back `is_rotation_valid: False`, `rotation_correction: 90`, and after the counter-clockwise turn the text is exact.

### olmOCR

Prompt `build_no_anchoring_v4_yaml_prompt()`, text part first, max_tokens 8000 as upstream (the engine uses 4096 and 8000 on retry, see below).

| Fixture (1288 px longest side) | Result | Prompt tokens | Generated | Server time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| legal_scan, full page | case no., 4 amounts exact; footer and Bates dropped, as in Phase 0 | 1786 | 394 | 15.7 s |
| two_column, full page | 30/30 lines, 29/29 in order | 1786 | 365 | 14.9 s |
| two_column, 3 Phase 2b crops | 30/30, 29/29 in order | 360 / 1326 / 1694 | 37 / 202 / 187 | 21.8 s total |
| narrow_unequal_seed2, full page | 42/42 lines, 41/41 in order | 1786 | 1048 | 32.3 s |
| narrow_unequal_seed2, 2 crops | 42/42, 41/41 in order | 1280 / 866 | 653 / 427 | 34.0 s total |
| transcript_full | Q./A. right, **line numbers dropped: 0/25 exact** | 1786 | 297 | 13.2 s |
| four_up | **100/100 exact** | 1786 | 1359 | 40.3 s |

**Plan decision (rule: use full page, unless crops bring line recall to at least 95% where full page is below 95%).** Full page is at 100% on both `two_column` and `narrow_unequal_seed2`, so the rule keeps the full page. Crops stay as the first answer to a loop only.

**Transcripts.** olmOCR scores 100/125 (80%) on the two transcript fixtures, below 95%, and 0/25 on the full-size page because it drops the margin line numbers. The stderr transcript hint therefore also points olmOCR users to `--model paddleocr-vl` (the engine's `transcript_hint`).

**Rates** (server log "Request completed", 13 requests): prefill 321 to 329 tok/s on image prompts (247 tok/s on the smallest crop, 55 tok/s on the 27-token probe, which is not a rate); decode 39.3 to 40.1 tok/s. The first request after the server started took 20.1 s for 397 tokens, about 4 s more than the same request later. Image cost is a constant 1786 prompt tokens for a 995x1288 page.
- A normal page generates 300 to 1400 tokens (13 to 40 s); `max_tokens` is 4096, because the densest fixtures stay under 1400 tokens, with 8000 on a `length` retry (olmOCR's own pipeline limit).
- Timeout = 2 x (prefill + max_tokens / decode) = 2 x (5.5 + 4096 / 39.5) = **218 s, catalog 220 s**; retry at 8000 tokens: 2 x (5.5 + 8000 / 39.5) = 416 s, **catalog 420 s**. Both live in `engines::limits`, with Paddle's values (4096 / 8192 / 45 s) moved there unchanged.

### Engine decisions in the implementation

- **Loop detector and tables.** The Paddle detector (a 10 to 120 character unit repeated 6 times) fires on a long HTML table with similar rows, so tables are cut out before it runs; a runaway table still ends as a `length` reply. Negative test: an 80-row table of identical rows is not flagged.
- **`length`** retries once with 8000 tokens, then the page falls back to Apple and is flagged (Paddle's behaviour); **loop** goes to the crop plan if there is one, else retries once with `repetition_penalty 1.15`, then falls back.
- **Empty output** (generic, all engines): the request is retried once; a page whose requests are all empty falls back to Apple and is flagged.
- **Rotation.** One retry on the turned full page; the crop plan is skipped on a turned page. If the page is still invalid after the turn, the text is kept and the page flagged.
- **Known limit.** olmOCR drops the footer, and the Apple side-pass cannot read a sideways page, so a rotated page gets no Bates number in its marker (the real rotated-fixture test checks the five body tokens only).

### dots

`dots.mocr-8bit`, `prompt_layout_all_en` verbatim, image first (as in Phase 0), 200 DPI (1700x2200), max_tokens 8192 in the spike.

| Fixture | Result | Prompt tokens | Generated | Server time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| legal, legal_scan, full page | all six tokens exact, footer and Bates kept (as `Page-footer`) | 5035 | 778 | 34.0 s |
| two_column, full page | 30/30 lines, 29/29 in order | 5035 | 1429 | 39.2 s |
| two_column, 3 crops | 30/30, 29/29 in order | 285 / 1438 / 1861 | 40 / 689 / 674 | 19.8 s total |
| narrow_unequal_seed2, full page | 42/42 lines, 41/41 in order | 5035 | 2537 | 48.3 s |
| narrow_unequal_seed2, 2 crops | 42/42, 41/41 in order | 2732 / 1896 | 1357 / 1111 | 33.9 s total |
| transcript_full | **25/25 exact** | 5035 | 369 | 30.7 s |
| four_up | **100/100 exact** | 5035 | 1732 | 41.7 s |

**Plan decision (same rule).** Full page is at 100% on both column fixtures, so the plan is the full page; crops are the first answer to a loop or a cut-off reply only.

**Transcripts.** 25/25 and 100/100, above 95%: no extra hint for dots, and the real-model test asserts the scores.

**Rates** (server log "Request completed", 20 requests): prefill 183 tok/s at 5035 prompt tokens (27.5 s), faster for smaller images (263 tok/s at 2930, 398 tok/s at 1386); decode 124 to 127 tok/s on the full page, up to 151 tok/s on short crops. No other process was using the GPU (see the load note above).
- **DPI cost** on `legal_scan` (tokens exact at all three): 200 DPI 5035 prompt tokens and 34.1 s; 150 DPI 2930 tokens and 17.1 s; 100 DPI 1386 tokens and 9.1 s. The default stays 200 as specified; lowering it is a Phase 6 tuning decision, with these costs as the input.
- `max_tokens` is 8192 as in Phase 0: the densest fixture used 2537 tokens, and a dots reply is verbose JSON, so a dense page could pass 4096. There is no larger retry for dots (a cut-off reply goes to crops).
- Timeout = 2 x (prefill + max_tokens / decode) = 2 x (27.5 + 8192 / 125) = **186 s, catalog 190 s** (same for crops and `prompt_ocr`, which are smaller).

**Reply shape.** A bare JSON array with no code fence in practice (the parser accepts one). bboxes are in pixels of the image sent and are not used. `Title` text comes without a `#` and may hold two lines (the court caption); a heading is one line, so lines are joined with a space. Tables are `<table><thead><tr><td>...` (header cells are `td`, so the first row is the header). The transcript came back as one `Text` element with `\n` between lines, line numbers kept.

**Ladder as built.**
1. Layout request on the page. A valid array becomes Markdown.
2. Invalid or cut-off JSON that ended with `stop`: retry once; if it stays invalid, the complete elements of the better reply are kept and the page is flagged. With no complete element it counts as a loop.
3. A loop (detector on the extracted text fields, tables cut out) or `finish_reason: length`: the crop plan if the page has one, then `prompt_ocr` as plain text on the page, then Apple Vision with a flag. A reply cut off by `length` is not kept as partial elements: crops and `prompt_ocr` are tried first and Apple's complete page beats a partial one.
4. `repetition_penalty` is never sent. A page answered by `prompt_ocr` is not flagged (it is a normal answer, but without headers, footers or structure; Bates still comes from the side-pass).

## Phase 3: long-document pipeline (2026-10-08)

### 300-page benchmark (apple defaults, nothing else running)

`spike/out/bench300/big.pdf` is `three_pages.pdf` x 100, run with `/usr/bin/time -l`:

| Run | Wall time | Peak memory footprint |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline (Phase 2b, vmmap) | 29 s | 470 MB |
| Phase 3, clean run (all pages checkpointed, then assembled from the records) | 28.4 s (10.6 pages/s) | 487 MB (max RSS 737 MB) |
| Phase 3, SIGKILL at 151 checkpoints, then re-run | 14.3 s (149 pages OCR'd, 151 resumed) | 491 MB |

Checkpointing and assembly from disk cost nothing measurable in time and about 17 MB of footprint.

### Live `--jobs` check (real servers, temp state dir, `three_pages.pdf`, 3 pages)

| Engine | `--jobs 1` | `--jobs 8` | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| olmocr (8-bit) | 47.0 s | 46.9 s | identical apart from `generated:` |
| dots-ocr (dots.mocr 8-bit) | 108.0 s | 108.0 s | identical apart from `generated:` |
| paddleocr-vl (1.6 bf16) | 14.3 s | 14.3 s | identical apart from `generated:` |

For model engines this tests side-pass and assembly concurrency, not model batching: requests are capped at the server's `--max-num-seqs` (1), so `--jobs 8` makes the same one-at-a-time requests as `--jobs 1` and prints the cap note.

## Apple Vision concurrent start-up crash (TextRecognition)

**Signature** (ten `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/ocr-2026-10-08-*.ips`, including one during a model-engine eval): `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` (SIGSEGV) in `libobjc objc_retain`, called from Apple's private `TextRecognition` framework, called from `Vision`, on `com.apple.root.default-qos.cooperative`, with 3-10 threads inside `TextRecognition` (others in `objc_sync_enter`, CoreML `MLLoader`, ANE `doLoadModel`). **Every real crash happened within 0.81 s of launch; none happened mid-run.**

**Repro**: `spike/repro_init_race.sh [iterations] [threads] [bench|scan]` launches fresh processes (default `vision_bench legal_300dpi.png 10`) and counts crash exits (139 SIGSEGV, 138 SIGBUS, 132 SIGILL, 133 SIGTRAP); in `scan` mode it also counts the supervisor's "Apple Vision crashed" notes.

| Variant (10 simultaneous requests, `vision_bench`) | Launches | SIGSEGV |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 300 | 14 (4.7%) |
| First request alone (NSLock gate) | 300 | 10 (3.3%) |
| Gate plus one extra serial warm call | 100 | 6 |
| One warm call, 2.5 s idle, then 10 threads | 100 | 8 |
| Gate, thread starts staggered by 150 ms | 100 | 1 |
| Cap of 2 concurrent requests | 100 | 0 |
| Cap of 1 concurrent request | 100 | 0 |

**Conclusion.** The root cause is in Apple's framework. The trigger is concurrent request start-up: with the first-use gate open, the crash comes in the wave right after the first call finishes (the dumps show 9 threads past the gate and none in it), and a completed warm call, even followed by 2.5 s idle, does not help. A first-use gate and warm-up therefore do not fix it. A cap of 2 looks effective (0 in 100) but costs about 1.5x on 16 images (3-4 s uncapped, 5-7 s cap 2, 9-11 s cap 1; noisy, shared machine). 0 in 100 is not proof, since 0 of 100 at a 4.7% rate happens by chance about 0.8% of the time.

**Decision.** The user chose cap 2 for prevention, plus a supervisor for containment:
- `bridge/Sources/OcrBridge/OcrBridge.swift`: a process-wide semaphore of 2 around every Vision request (`blocking()`); `OCR_VISION_MAX_CONCURRENT` (1-64) overrides it for measurement. `--jobs` keeps its meaning (worker threads); rendering and the rest overlap while Vision recognizes at most 2 pages at a time.
- `src/supervisor.rs`: a non-dry-run `ocr scan` re-executes itself as a child. If the child dies from SIGSEGV, SIGBUS, SIGILL or SIGTRAP it prints `note: Apple Vision crashed (signal N); resuming from checkpoints (retry k of 3)` and runs again, resuming from the per-page checkpoints. At most 3 retries; SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGKILL are never retried; the child's exit code is passed through. The parent handles SIGINT with a no-op handler (the child gets Ctrl-C from the terminal's process group), forwards SIGTERM/SIGHUP, and the child exits if the parent is killed. A retry keeps the crashed run's checkpoints even with `--overwrite`; in a directory scan, files that finished before the crash are redone.
- Tests: `tests/supervisor.rs` injects crashes with `OCR_TEST_CRASH_AFTER=N` (after N checkpoints; `OCR_TEST_CRASH_ATTEMPTS`, `OCR_TEST_CRASH_SIGNAL`) and reads the in-flight peak through `OCR_TEST_VISION_STATS`.

## Transcript line-number re-anchoring (2026-10-08)

**Problem.** A deposition transcript numbers every *physical* line 1-25, wrapped continuations included (`6 Q. Did you ever agree to extend the payment` then `7 deadline?`). Every engine reads the words well, but the models join a continuation onto the line above and renumber their output sequentially, so every number after a wrap is wrong and page:line citations break. Before this change, exact `N text` lines on eval seeds 10-12 (`transcript4up`): dots 68%, Apple 38%, olmOCR 30%, Paddle 25%.

**Method** (`src/anchor.rs`; transcript-flagged pages only, every engine including Apple). The numbers come from page geometry, never from the model:

1. **Mini-pages.** A header pass reads the whole sheet at 200 DPI and finds the `Page N` labels (fuzzy: Vision reads `Fage 42`). A 2x2 (or any 2+ cell) sheet becomes one cell per grid position, with the grid completed when a label is missing (cell edges at the midpoints between label columns, and just above each label row). A page with fewer than two labels is one region. The Phase 2b regions are **not** used: on eval sheets they find two full-height columns, not quadrants. Each cell is then recognized on its own at 300 DPI with the bridge's new `lines` option (`DocumentObservation.Container.Text.lines`: `[{text, bbox}]` per page, normalized, top-left origin, mapped back to page coordinates for crops). Whole-sheet Vision lines on a 4-up sheet at 200 DPI are mostly garbage, a quadrant crop is nearly perfect. Mini-pages are ordered by their `Page N` number.
2. **Slot grid.** Vision lines that start with a 1-25 number (a separate observation, or glued to the text; a glued number must start left of where plain text starts) are fitted by y = a + b·n with the median of pairwise slopes (Theil-Sen) and the median intercept, discarding points more than 0.4 pitch off and refitting. Accepted with at least 5 distinct inlier numbers, median residual under 0.15 pitch and a pitch of 0.4-8% of the region. Otherwise the typical line pitch (median of the small gaps between text lines) is placed with at least two consistent numbers; if that fails too, the region is unverified.
3. **Physical lines.** Each remaining Vision line goes to the slot nearest its y-centre (pieces of one slot are joined left to right); a number prefix that agrees with the grid is stripped. A line far from every slot stays an unnumbered line.
4. **Alignment.** The engine's text, with its own leading numbers and `Page N` lines removed, is tokenized to words and aligned to the Vision word stream of all regions with word-level Needleman-Wunsch (similarity = 1 - edit distance / length; two words match at 0.5; a mismatch costs less than two gaps, so `Q.` against Vision's `l.` still lines up). The engine may read the regions in any order, so every order of up to 4 regions is tried and the best alignment wins. Each engine word takes the physical line of the Vision word it aligns to; unaligned engine words join the previous line, or the next one if they start a line of the engine's own. Output is `N <engine words>`: the engine's words, `Q.`/`A.`/`MR. X:` prefixes and all, with the geometry's numbers. For Apple the engine text is the Vision lines themselves, so Apple also moves to per-mini-page crops.
5. **Confidence.** A region needs at least 80% of its engine words and 80% of its Vision words matched; otherwise that region keeps the engine's own lines. A page with any such region (or with no credible grid, or no readable geometry) is `unverified`. Front matter: `line_numbers: {anchored: [pages], unverified: [pages]}`, only present when the document has transcript pages (so the other goldens are byte-identical).
6. **Paddle** sends each mini-page of a multi-up sheet as a crop (4 requests, in `Page N` order) instead of the whole sheet; a full-page transcript stays one request. Other engines keep their request plans.

**Bug found on the way.** The bridge decoded its options with a non-optional `lines` key; a request without the key failed to decode and silently reset every option (language correction back to on). The key is now optional on the Swift side and always sent by Rust. The four goldens (`legal`, `legal_scan`, `two_column`, `three_pages`) are byte-identical.

**Tests.** `src/anchor.rs`: slot fit with missing numbers and outliers, pitch fallback, wrapped continuation gets its own number, typo-heavy Vision still aligns, low coverage is unverified, engine reading order and missing headers, ordering by `Page N`, grid completion. Fake-server (`tests/paddle.rs`): a fake reply with merged wraps and sequential renumbering (served from `FAKE_REPLIES`) comes out with exactly the ground-truth numbering, from four crop requests; a non-matching reply is kept and marked unverified. Apple (`tests/apple.rs`): `transcript_full.pdf` and `four_up.pdf`.

**Measured** (`eval/anchor_eval.py`, scored with `eval/score.py`: exact `N text` lines of `transcript4up`; tune = seeds 0-2, accept = seeds 10-12, run once).

Exact `N text` lines, `transcript4up` family (`eval/anchor_eval.py`, scored with `eval/score.py`):

| Engine | Before (seeds 10-12) | Held-out, seeds 40-42 (run once, thresholds frozen) | Seeds 10-12 (run once, then retuned: no longer held out) | Tune seeds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dots-ocr | 68% | **99.9%** (699/700) | not run | 0-2 offline replay of earlier whole-sheet output: 42.4% to 99.8% |
| Apple | 38% | **97.4%** (682/700) | 98.1% (883/900) | 0-2: 97.1% |
| olmOCR | 30% | **99.9%** (699/700) | not run | n/a |
| PaddleOCR-VL | 25% | **94.9%** (664/700), **misses the 95% target** | 92.0% (828/900), engine coverage threshold 0.8 | 0-2: 95.4%; 3-9: 94.0% to 95.2% |

Sheets unverified (fallback rate): 0 of 7 on seeds 40-42 for every engine. On seeds 10-12 Paddle had 1 unverified sheet of 9 (a mini-page where the model repeated and invented lines); with the final engine-coverage threshold such pages are anchored.

**Tuning (seeds 0-9 only).** Paddle crop DPI, seeds 0-2: 150: 90.4%; 175: 93.5%; 200: 95.4%; 225: 90.2% (one seed failed); 250: 75.8%; 300: 84.9%. At high DPI Paddle drops or repeats lines. Transcript crops therefore render at no less than 200 DPI (`TRANSCRIPT_CROP_DPI`). Engine-side coverage threshold, Paddle seeds 3-9: 0.8: 94.0%; 0.5: 95.2%. A region needs 80% of its Vision words but only 50% of its engine words matched, because a model that repeats or invents lines leaves extra engine words that align to nothing while the lines it did read are still placed reliably. Dots and olmOCR were not re-tuned.

**Paddle misses 95% on held-out seeds 40-42 (94.9%).** The remaining misses are the model's, not the numbering's: it drops whole lines, repeats a line three times, invents extra Q lines, or reads `Q.` as another letter. The engine's words are kept as produced, so those lines cannot become exact. Of the 36 inexact lines, a loose check finds the text elsewhere on the page for 23 (usually because the model dropped or duplicated a line, shifting the following lines, and the text repeats in the transcript), and the text wrong or missing for 13.

**Notes.**
- The stderr transcript hints were updated afterwards (40562ab). Apple now says line numbers were re-anchored, points to `line_numbers.unverified` and recommends dots-ocr. Model engines warn only when a transcript page could not be re-anchored.
- A `Page N` header is added from Vision's reading when the engine put several mini-pages on one sheet; for a single-region page it is only kept if the engine wrote one.
- Dots and olmOCR read the whole sheet; their regions may come out in any order (all orders of up to 4 regions are tried) and the output is always in `Page N` order.
- `examples/anchor_replay.rs` re-anchors saved engine output offline; `eval/anchor_diag.py` classifies misses.

## Column split false positives on real filings (2026-10-08)

The public court-filing set (eval/PUBLIC_SET.md) showed Apple splitting single-column pages into columns and cutting lines mid-word. `examples/split_survey.rs` runs the side pass (150 DPI, regions at 100 DPI) on every page (first 60 per document) and lists the pages with two or more column regions.

Three causes, measured with a temporary chain dump:

- **Drifting cuts.** A gutter candidate is tracked strip to strip with 5 px of drift allowed. On typewriter text and ragged captions, word spaces and line ends overlap pairwise but no straight channel runs through all four strips (Lozano p3: `lo=455 hi=127`; Knight p1: `lo=417 hi=217`). The old code then cut at the mean midpoint, which runs through words. Every true split measured had a straight channel (7-167 px).
- **Pleading margins wider than 0.08.** Line numbers plus sideways court-name text or form numbers reach 0.085-0.134 of the page width (Garland, Ironworkers, Lozano p1), so the strip became a column.
- **Q/A marker strips.** Full-page transcripts have a 0.013-0.025-wide strip of Q and A markers that was split off as its own column (Knight, 12 pages).

Fix (`src/regions.rs`):
- a gutter must be one straight channel through all four strips (`lo < hi`), cut at its middle;
- `MIN_GUTTER` is 0.02 of the page width (was 0.012). Courier word spaces line up into straight rivers 11-14 px wide at 100 DPI; real gutters measured 17-167 px (a skewed one had a 7 px common channel with 22 px runs);
- a margin strip (dropped when the page is split) must be under 0.14 of the page width (was 0.08), span at least half the page height, sit in the edge zone, and be under half as wide as the widest piece of the cut. The last two rules came from checking every Column-to-Margin flip: an absolute 0.14 alone dropped the first column of a landscape table (Nissan p27) and the first words of a Courier paragraph (Nissan p15);
- a piece narrower than 0.05 of the page width that is not a margin joins its neighbour instead of becoming a column. Table columns at 0.053-0.054 (Nissan p27) are just above this; a table with narrower columns is read whole by Vision rather than split.

Four new unit tests (a drifting typewriter river, a Q/A marker strip, six narrow table columns, and a short narrow edge piece) each fail with their rule removed.

| Set | Pages split before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Public filings, 25 documents (first 60 pages each) | 119 | 71 |
| of which Knight transcript / Garland order / Ironworkers order / Lozano | 13 / 13 / 10 / 4 | 0 / 1 / 1 / 2 |
| Synthetic fixtures and seeds 10-12 | 10 pages | the same 10 pages |

Every remaining Margin on the public set was rendered and holds only line numbers, a form stamp or scan specks. The remaining splits are side-by-side caption, signature and index blocks and 4-up transcripts. The only synthetic change: on `four_up.pdf` each mini-page's line-number strip now stays with its text (before, the left one was a margin and the right one a column of its own). Apple transcript lines on held-out seeds 40-42 are unchanged at 682/700 (97.4%). All goldens are byte-identical. Lozano p3 now reads as whole lines; Knight p6 is no longer split, but it is still not detected as a transcript (separate follow-up).

## llama-server spike (2026-10-08, Linux, PLAN §9 Phase 7a/7d-1)

**Setup.** llama.cpp b11510 (`ubuntu-vulkan-x64` and `ubuntu-x64` CPU builds) on this Linux box: Ryzen 9950X, integrated Radeon (RADV RAPHAEL_MENDOCINO), 30 GB RAM, no NVIDIA. Model `PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL-1.6-GGUF` (BF16, plus mmproj). Pages were rendered through the production path (`examples/render_png`, pdfium). The request had the same shape as `model_engine::post`: image first, then text, temperature 0, `max_tokens` 4096.

**Results.**
- **Output matches the MLX output in kind.**
  - `OCR:` on `legal.pdf` at 150 DPI found all 7 checked values exactly: case number, four amounts, Bates `SMITH000123`, and the footer.
  - `legal_scan.pdf` gave the same text.
  - Vulkan and CPU outputs were byte-identical.
  - `Table Recognition:` returns OTSL (`<fcel>…<nl>`).
  - `finish_reason` was `stop`, with no leftover template tokens.
  - 1253 prompt tokens, 299 completion tokens.
- **No template flag is needed.** Jinja is on by default, and llama-server maps `image_url` to its own media marker. `/health` answers in about 2 s.
- **Speed on this machine:**

  | Build | Per page | Notes |
  |---|---|---|
  | CPU | 7.5 s | Prompt about 320 tok/s, decode about 83 tok/s |
  | Vulkan on the integrated GPU | 46 s | Image encoding takes 40–50 s of that |

  **On integrated graphics the CPU build is about 6x faster.** 7e must prefer CPU there.
- **`-np 2`:** both concurrent requests were correct. 1.25x faster on CPU, no gain on Vulkan.
- **Memory:** with no `--ctx-size`, each slot gets the model's full 131072-token context, and the CPU build peaks at 4.5 GB (6.9 GB with 2 slots). `ocr` now sizes `--ctx-size` per engine x slots: **2.1 GB resident** with the CPU build.
- **Archive layout:** everything is flat in `llama-b11510/`. `llama-server` is a small launcher with its `.so` files (symlink chains included) beside it; `ocr` adds that directory to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
- **Through `ocr` itself:** `ocr server setup --model paddleocr-vl` downloads, verifies and unpacks llama.cpp, pdfium and the GGUFs. `server start` is then ready in 3.4 s (Vulkan) or 0.8 s (CPU), and `status` and `stop` work.
- **Not tested:** `repetition_penalty` (the loop retry), olmOCR, dots, CUDA.

## olmOCR footer strip and Bates corners (2026-10-08, Linux CPU build, PLAN §9.5)

**Setup.** olmOCR 2, Q4_K_M GGUF, llama.cpp b11510 CPU build. Prompt: the upstream v4 prompt, text first. Images: 1288 px on the longest side.

**Footer strip: fails.** The bottom 10% or 15% of `legal.pdf` and `legal_scan.pdf` came back as front matter and nothing else (31 tokens), even though the strip clearly shows `COMPLAINT - Page 1 of 14` and `SMITH000123`. The front matter itself was valid (`is_rotation_valid: True`). A plain "transcribe everything" prompt returned the footer line but still dropped the Bates number. olmOCR treats the strip as page furniture.

**Bottom-right corner alone (`0.7, 0.9, 0.3, 0.1`): works.** It returned `SMITH000123` with the normal prompt.

**Implemented (your decision):** off the Mac, when the page text has no Bates number, olmOCR gets the bottom-right corner and then the bottom-left corner (`0.0, 0.9, 0.3, 0.1`). Each request is capped at 256 tokens, and the first Bates match wins. Results through `ocr scan`:

| Test | Bates in marker |
|---|---|
| `legal.pdf` (bottom right) | `SMITH000123` |
| `legal_scan.pdf` (scan, bottom right) | `SMITH000123` |
| `three_pages.pdf` (page 2 has none) | 1 and 3: `SMITH000123`; 2: none. Matches the Mac golden |
| `legal.pdf` restamped bottom left `DEF000456` | `DEF000456` |
| `legal.pdf` restamped bottom centre `ABC000789`, under the footer | **none**. A known limit: a centred Bates is not covered |
| eval `production` seed 10, pages 1–4 (bottom right, Helvetica) | `ACME0000001`–`ACME0000004`, all correct |

**Cost:** about 52 s a page against about 40 s without the corners, on the CPU build. On a GPU each corner should take about a second. A page with no Bates number pays for both corners.

**Scanned pages are the remaining Azure load.** A free local second reader is queued next to address it (docs/overnight-report.md, follow-ups).

## Exact characters from embedded text, with Vision's layout (2026-10-09)

Apple's default `--use-text-layer auto` keeps Vision's blocks (layout, tables, margin numbers, Bates) and aligns each block's words with the PDF's embedded text inside the block's box. A new bridge call, `ocr_bridge_text_in_regions`, inverts the render transform and works on rotated pages. The alignment is in `src/embedded.rs`. Its safeguards:
- **Page gate:** at least 90% word agreement on the page, or nothing changes.
- **Per-word check:** a differing word is replaced only when it looks like a misread, with at most a third of its characters different.
- **No inserted text:** embedded text that Vision did not see is never added. This covers redactions, hidden text, and neighbours caught by a box.
- **Skipped for now:** column-split and transcript pages.

Measured on the 20 public filings (230 pages, Apple, 150 DPI), against the earlier pure-OCR run:

| | Pure OCR | Default `auto` |
|---|---|---|
| Born-digital pages corrected | - | 95 of 139 |
| Partly born-digital pages corrected | - | 13 of 28 |
| Words changed to the embedded form | - | 1,350 |
| Output words found in the embedded text (born-digital) | 90.1% | 90.7% |
| Output words found in the embedded text (partial) | 98.0% | 98.4% |
| `--verify-json` pages in `azure_pages` | 61 | 51 |
| Of which e-filed / partial / scanned | 18 / 9 / 34 | 15 / 2 / 34 |
| Values verified free | 576 | 601 |

**The word-match share is a weak metric here,** because it rises only a little. Vision's own output carries margin numbers and headers that the embedded text orders or spells differently, and the 44 uncorrected born-digital pages are either column-split or transcript pages, or below the 90% page gate.

**Sample corrections:**
- `Califomia` to `California`;
- `SZA` to `S2A` (a company name);
- `S10` and `S8` to `$10` and `$8`;
- `mıkulicm(@)sec.gov` to `mikulicm@sec.gov`;
- straight quotes to the filing's curly quotes.

**Goldens:** the pure-OCR goldens (`--use-text-layer never`) are byte-identical apart from the new empty `embedded_text_fixes: {}` line. A new test checks the default output on legal.pdf: the golden with `Case No.3:26-cv-04417` corrected to `Case No. 3:26-cv-04417`.

## `--verify-json` compares values, not substrings (2026-10-09)

A review found that `verified` meant "the squashed text occurs somewhere in the embedded text", so `$3,000` was verified by `$3,000,000` and `3:26-cv-0441` by `3:26-cv-04417`. Now each field and the embedded text are reduced to the same canonical keys:
- amount in cents;
- ISO date;
- docket as office, year, kind and number;
- squashed text for Bates numbers and citations.

A field is `verified` only when its key is among the embedded text's keys. The embedded text is flattened first, so a date or amount broken across lines still matches. Docket keys also match without the office prefix.

**Look-alike characters:** amounts, dates and dockets that mix digits with `O o I l S B Q` get `confusable_characters` and no `value`. They are never verified. An error-injection test plants 16 misreads into a page whose embedded text has the true values: look-alike letters, one-digit changes, and `$3,000` for `$3,000,000`. It checks that none comes back `verified`.

**Scale words:** `$45` at the end of a line followed by `million` on the next (past one blank line or a pleading line number) is the amount `$45 million`. `K`/`M`/`B` suffixes are scales. `$1,50B` stays a malformed amount.

Measured on the 20 public filings (Apple, default `auto`), against the substring check:

| | Substrings | Values |
|---|---|---|
| Pages in `azure_pages` | 51 | 53 |
| Values verified free | 601 | 602 |
| No longer verified | - | 3 |
| Newly verified | - | 4 |

**The three values no longer verified:**
- `CV-00886` twice: a false Bates match (the text is part of a docket number);
- `$246.95` on a scanned loan form, where the embedded text has `246 95` with the cents in a separate box.

Both outcomes are the safe direction. The newly verified values are amounts whose scale word was on the next line.

## Second reader for scanned pages (2026-10-09)

`--verify-json` now reads each page that has values but no embedded text a second time. The bridge gained a `reader: "text"` option. It runs Vision's older `RecognizeTextRequest` (line level, accurate, no language correction) at 300 DPI, and returns lines with confidence and the next-best readings. Two re-reads run at a time, within the bridge's Vision limit.

**Confidence and alternatives carry no signal in accurate mode.** On 732 lines of a scanned motion, confidence was 1.0 on every line, and no line had an alternative. The doubtful check (confidence below 0.5, or a next-best reading that changes the value) is kept because it costs nothing, but in practice it does not fire.

**Measured blind on born-digital pages.** The pages were OCRed with `--use-text-layer never`, and the embedded text was hidden from verify (`OCR_VERIFY_IGNORE_EMBEDDED=1`), so the second reader decided alone. Its decisions were graded against the run that could see the embedded text. 20 public filings, 230 pages:

| | Values |
|---|---|
| Values the embedded text confirms | 574 |
| Of these, flagged by the second reader (false alarms) | 27 (4.7%) |
| Values the embedded text contradicts | 47 |
| Of these, flagged by the second reader | 21 (45%) |

**Agreement between two Apple readings proved not independent.** Before agreement was demoted, 546 values were confirmed this way, and 25 of them disagreed with the embedded text. Most of those 25 were cases where the embedded text was itself wrong or misparsed:
- a 1985 scan with an old OCR text layer;
- a handwritten form;
- a footnote marker stuck to an amount, `$1,000,000.8`.

Eight were real shared errors. A Jane Street filing carries two overprinted stamps, `Filed 04/24/24` and `Filed 04/18/24`, and both Apple readers read the blend as `04/28/24`, a date in neither stamp.

**Hence:** on Apple pages the second reading only finds disagreements. Agreement verifies a value only when the first reading came from a model engine, and the page did not fall back to Apple.

**Symbol repair:** the second reading gets the same `§`/`¶` restoration as the first. Without it, `S 1983` was a disagreement with `§ 1983`. Restoring the symbols cut false alarms from 46 to 27, and catches went from 22 to 21. Bare pleading line numbers are dropped before matching, because they come between `May 7,` and `2007.`. `S5,500` counts as `$5,500` when the amount has digit grouping or cents.

**Default run** (Apple, `auto`, 20 filings), compared with master:
- **Pages in `azure_pages`:** 53 → 55. Nine values on scans are now `check` rather than `unchecked`. Three of them are `§` misread as `$` (`$1446`, `$ 1983`, `$2254`).
- **Time:** 125 s → 144 s for the whole set; 60 pages were re-read.

**Not yet measured:** a live model run. The model path (agreement verifies) is unit-tested only.

## Whole-text agreement (2026-10-09)

`--verify-json` now reports, per page, which sentences another reading has word for word (`text_agreement`, `src/agreement.rs`). This tells a tool which wording it can quote.
- **Spans:** sentences, or whole lines when shorter. Abbreviations like `No.`, `U.S.C.` and `Inc.` do not end a sentence.
- **Comparison:** words are compared as letters and digits, case-insensitively, in order, and with nothing between them.

Each rule below came from a failure on the public filings, or from the error-injection test, which changes, drops or doubles every word of a reference passage in turn:
- **Pleading line numbers** may be skipped, but only structurally:
  - in the other reading, when they stand alone on a line or start one;
  - in the Markdown, only at the start of a line.

  A number inside a line is never skipped, so `30` read for `80` still differs, and so does a `30` that only the OCR has. That matters because a model can invent a number.
- **Edges:** in prose (a span ending in sentence punctuation), the span must start and end at a sentence or line edge of the other reading. A span that follows another sentence in the Markdown must follow a sentence end there too. Without this, a sentence missing its first word ("Not later than…" read as "later than…") agreed, and so did a doubled `2024.` at a line start. Headers and table cells are exempt, because Vision splits them where the PDF has one line.
- **Margin legends:** PDFKit puts the vertical left-margin legend ("United States District Court / Northern District of California") between a paragraph's lines. A whole line of the other reading may be skipped inside a match only if it has at least three words, and the Markdown has it on another line. A line the OCR dropped is not elsewhere in the Markdown, so it still breaks agreement (tested).

**Measured on the 20 public filings** (Apple, default `auto`):

| Pages | Compared with | Sentences agreed | Median words agreed per page |
|---|---|---|---|
| Born-digital (139) | embedded text | 77.2% | 90% |
| Partly born-digital (28) | embedded text | 91.4% | 94% |
| Scanned (59) | second Apple reading, not independent | 64.6% | 64% |

**What remains unagreed on born-digital pages:**
- real differences: OCR misreads (`Issu`, `It'l`) on pages the embedded correction does not touch;
- a 1985 scan whose text layer is itself bad OCR, and a handwritten form;
- condensed two-up transcripts, whose layout the PDF text orders differently.

All of these are the safe direction: a sentence that does not agree is not quoted as confirmed.

## Missing-text check (2026-10-09)

`text_agreement.missing_lines` lists the lines of the other reading (embedded text, or the second reader) that the OCR lacks entirely. A page with at least 5 such words gets `missing_text` in `page_check`.

**What counts as missing:** a line with at least 4 words, of which fewer than a third of the word pairs appear anywhere in the page's Markdown. A misread word spoils at most two pairs, so lines with OCR errors are not taken for missing ones.

**How the rule was reached:**
- The first rule was "no three-word run in common". It flagged 106 pages, because short lines with one misread (`prepare a detense.`) lost every run.
- Letter-spaced headings (`A P P E A R A N C E S`) are joined into one word.
- An error-injection test drops each line of a page in turn: each is reported, and the full page reports nothing.

**Measured on the 20 public filings** (Apple, default `auto`):
- **Pages with `missing_text`:** 88, of which 57 born-digital, 13 partly born-digital, and 18 scanned (against the second reader).
- **Spread:** more than a third of them are on two documents. One is a 1985 loan note whose text layer is itself bad OCR, which matches nothing (10 pages). The other is a bankruptcy filing whose "Created with Scanner Pro" stamp the OCR garbles on every page (15).
- **Real drops:** spot checks found Apple Vision skipped whole visible text.
  - On a two-column dealer agreement, the "ARTICLE NINTH: Execution of Agreement" paragraph is plainly printed and absent from the OCR.
  - On an order, a footnote citation (`278 F.Supp.2d 1079`) is missing.
- **Azure cost:** `azure_pages` went from 55 to 57. Born-digital pages with `missing_text` get `second_reading: embedded_text` when their values match, because the PDF's own text is the free second reading.

**Not yet measured:** precision over the whole set. It needs a labelled sample of flagged lines; the eval item in the queue will add it.

## Arithmetic checks (2026-10-09)

`src/arithmetic.rs` adds two checks to `--verify-json`. A mismatch adds its reason to `page_check` and to the amount fields involved. No value is ever changed.

**Amounts in words against numerals**, for example `Three Hundred Ninety Two Dollars and Thirty One Cents ($392.31)`, `four million dollars ($4 million)`, or `FORTY-FIVE THOUSAND AND NO/100 DOLLARS ($45,000.00)`.
- The words must name money (`dollars`, `cents`, `NN/100`), so `Section Two ($500 per day)` is not compared.
- An error-injection test changes a digit on either side, or a number word, and each change is caught.

**Table totals:** a row labelled total must equal the sum of the money cells above it in the same column, back to the header or the previous total.
- A `Subtotal` row is allowed for: the next total may equal the subtotals plus the rows after them (tax, fees).
- Cells count as money only with `$`, digit grouping or cents, so years and counts are not summed.
- An injection test changes each line item, and then the total; each change is caught.

**Public filings:** no mismatches. The two amounts in words in the set (`four million dollars ($4 million)` and `Three Hundred Ninety Two Dollars and Thirty One Cents ($392.31)`) agree with their numerals, and no table has a total row whose sum fails. Both checks are therefore exercised mostly by the synthetic tests.

## More case-number formats, and money without `$` (2026-10-09)

**Labelled case numbers:** the token after `Case No.`, `Civil Action No.`, `C.A. No.`, `Index No.`, `Cause No.` or `Adv. Proc. No.` is a docket field, in any court's format: `11-4604 PSG`, `C-08-01337 MHP`, `5215-VCG`, `20 Civ. 05382`, `651234/2021`.
- **Excluded:** `Docket No. 35` (an entry citation).
- **Matching:** these are compared as their exact letters and digits. A look-alike letter in a digit run (`C-O8-01337`) is still found, and gets `confusable_characters`.
- **Fragments:** a number cut off at a line end (`Case No. 03:11-`) is dropped, and so is anything with fewer than four digits. On the public filings, such fragments (`03:11`, `5:19`) had matched equally cut-off fragments in the embedded text.

**Money without `$`:** `USD 5,000`, `5,000 dollars`, and `sum|amount|total|price|fee|payment|balance of 5,000.00`. Cents are required in the last shape, because "amount of 1,500 units" is a count. These are compared by value with `$` amounts.

**Embedded text:** a hyphen at a line end now joins its halves before values are read (`5:15-` / `CV-01102-JGB-SP`), and soft hyphens are dropped. Without this, two correctly read case numbers were flagged.

**Public filings:**
- 23 more docket fields: 15 verified, 3 `unchecked` (on scans), and 5 `check`.
- One of the `check` values is a real disagreement: the OCR reads `5:15CV-01102-JGB` where the page has `5:15-CV-01102-JGB-SP`, a dropped hyphen.
- No amounts without `$` occur in the set, so that shape is exercised by tests only.

**Not done:** embedded-text correction on column-split and transcript pages. That changes the OCR text itself, and would need its own measurement against the Jev judge.
